intro.text: Sunstone Hotel Investors, Inc. (the “Company”) was incorporated in Maryland on June 28, 2004 in anticipation of an initial public offering of common stock, which was consummated on October 26, 2004. The Company elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust (“REIT”) for federal income tax purposes, commencing with its taxable year ended on December 31, 2004. The Company, through its 100 % controlling interest in Sunstone Hotel Partnership, LLC (the “Operating Partnership”), of which the Company is the sole managing member, and the subsidiaries of the Operating Partnership, including Sunstone Hotel TRS Lessee, Inc. (the “TRS Lessee”) and its subsidiaries, invests in hotels where it can add value through capital investment, hotel repositioning, and asset management.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

We rely on our hotel operators to adjust room rates and pricing for hotel services to reflect the effects of inflation.
We also rely on the foregoing entities as potential purchasers of hotels we seek to sell.

We and our third-party managers and franchisors rely on information technology networks and systems, including the internet, to access, process, transmit and store electronic customer and financial information.
In addition, we rely on the security systems of our third-party managers and franchisors to protect proprietary and customer information from these threats.
Because we are a REIT, we depend on third parties to operate our hotels, which could harm our results of operations.
These independent management companies control the daily operations of our hotels, and we rely on them to operate our hotels as provided in the applicable management agreements.
We rely on our corporate and hotel senior management teams, the loss of whom may cause us to incur costs and harm our business.

Because we are a REIT, we depend on the TRS Lessee and its subsidiaries to make rent payments to us, and their inability to do so could harm our revenue and our ability to make distributions to our stockholders.

We lease each of our hotels to the TRS Lessee or one of its subsidiaries, which engages with third-party eligible management companies to operate and manage all aspects of the properties; and those third-party managers, in turn, rely on systems that they manage directly or indirectly (through their own service providers), including but not limited to reservation systems, billing, building and property management systems, point-of-sale systems, and financial transactions and records that store and process proprietary or personal information.

In light of this structure, we do not have actual or contractual access to the systems or information maintained by the third-party managers, and we must instead rely on such managers’ programs and processes to protect the properties in which we invest from risks associated with cybersecurity threats.

We strongly encourage investors to review our financial information in its entirety and not to rely on a single financial measure.
